events.content:
## Result

**Evidence score: withheld. `evidence_strength` = QUALITY-LIMITED.**

This is **not** a low score — no normalised score was produced at all. The summary tool suppressed it because the locus failed the mapping-quality gate.

### Why it was withheld

`bam_stats_at_locus` over chr20:25,799,500–25,800,500 (IMP10) returned:
- 206 reads, mean depth 25.96
- **mean MAPQ 0.0, low-MAPQ fraction 1.00 (100%)**
- strand balance even (103 forward / 103 reverse)

The summary's quality gate fires when >40% of reads are below MAPQ 20; here it is 100.0%. Every read at this position is ambiguously mapped, so the region is effectively repetitive and the evidence layers cannot be trusted.

### What the layers reported (all at min_mapq 20 unless noted)

| Layer | Result |
|---|---|
| Discordant pairs | 0 — all 206 reads in the ±500bp window fell below MAPQ 20 |
| Soft clips | 0 — all 94 reads below MAPQ 20; no consensus clip position |
| Split reads (min_mapq **20**) | 0 — all 92 reads below MAPQ 20 |
| Split reads (min_mapq **0**, separate call) | 2 SA-tagged reads (fraction 0.022), partners at chr22_KI270733v1_random:38854 and chr21:7599999 — one per chromosome, i.e. scattered, not a cluster |
| Read depth | min/mean ratio 0.606, `likely_deletion` true, dip at 25,800,000 (0bp from focus) |

`signal_layers`: 0/4. Raw score 0.0/100, explicitly flagged "for reference only".

Two cautions on those last two rows:
- The split-read tool defaults to **min_mapq 0**, which is why it showed 2 reads the summary (min_mapq 20) discarded. Those 2 reads point to two *different* partner chromosomes, including an unplaced random contig — that is the signature of mismapping in a repeat, not of a junction.
- The depth layer counts **all** reads regardless of MAPQ, so it is the only layer still registering anything here. Its `likely_deletion: true` call rests entirely on reads that are themselves MAPQ 0, and should not be read as a deletion call.

### Also worth flagging

The position 25,800,000 was supplied directly in your question; it did **not** come from a registered candidate set. Nothing in these results corroborates that it is a real caller-derived junction — I have only characterised the locus you named. If there is a VCF for IMP10, loading it with `load_candidate_set` would establish whether any caller actually nominated a breakend here.

### Bottom line

The correct statement is: *the evidence score for chr20:25,800,000 in IMP10 was withheld under the QUALITY-LIMITED flag because 100% of reads there are below MAPQ 20.* The data cannot support either confirming or rejecting a breakpoint at this position; resolving it would need a technology with better mappability in this repeat (e.g. long reads), not a re-run of these layers.

I also want to note that the position was supplied by the caller rather than drawn from a candidate set.
